claims.text: The FeNiCrMn alloy is Co-free and derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The initial FeNiCrMn alloy is metastable and single-phase.
Removing Co increases lattice distortion in FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co alters local chemical order.
The changes caused by removing Co lower the effective stacking-fault energy.
Lower stacking-fault energy promotes deformation twinning.
At lower temperatures and higher strain rates, thermally activated dislocation glide has insufficient time to proceed completely.
Lower temperatures and higher strain rates shift deformation toward increased twinning in the Co-free alloy.
The Co-free alloy may exhibit enhanced dynamic strain aging at lower temperatures and higher strain rates.
Increased twinning boosts work hardening and strength.
At higher temperatures, thermal activation favors dislocation glide and dynamic recovery.
High-temperature dislocation glide and dynamic recovery increase ductility.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have higher work-hardening rates and strength at lower temperatures and higher strain rates.
The predicted low-temperature, high-strain-rate strengthening is associated with a greater incidence of twinning.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have greater ductility and lower strength at elevated temperatures.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the samples remain single-phase solid solutions.
Phase separation or precipitation at extreme temperatures or compositions may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
A controlled comparison of Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi at matched temperatures and strain rates can isolate the effect associated with Co removal.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that Co removal alters local chemical order and thereby lowers stacking-fault energy, whereas the structural-mediator field states that lattice distortion and modified stacking-fault energies influence local chemical ordering. This reverses or obscures the proposed causal ordering between local chemical order and stacking-fault energy.
